title: Flipping Alice's special bit negates it
statement: Let $\omega$ be a sample from the hard distribution, and write $X_T(\omega)$ for Alice's bit at the special coordinate of $\omega$. Let $\omega'$ be the sample obtained from $\omega$ by toggling Alice's special-coordinate bit while leaving all other data unchanged. Then $X_T(\omega') = \lnot\, X_T(\omega)$; that is, reading Alice's special bit after the flip yields the negation of Alice's special bit before it.
